She's With Me

Jessica Cunsolo

4.05
14,312 ratings1,359 reviews
Rate this book
Un nou oraş, o nouă dragoste, o nouă şansă de a rămâne în viaţă!

Atunci când Amelia Collins se mută într-un nou oraş cu o nouă identitate, ea plănuieşte să treacă neobservată şi să-şi încheie în linişte ultimul an de liceu. Dar totul se schimbă atunci când îl întâlneşte pe cel mai atrăgător băiat rău din şcoală, misteriosul Aiden Parker.

Curând, Amelia este integrată în grupul acestuia de prieteni, trezindu-se prinsă între noua viaţă şi încercarea de a lăsa în urmă un trecut tragic. Pe fondul unui an şcolar plin de prietenii noi şi vechi rivalităţi, Amelia se îndrăgosteşte de Aiden, care are propria poveste de viaţă întunecată. Numai că ea trebuie să lupte cu trăirile sale – la urma urmei, în ultimii ani de viaţă a fost o fugară.

Oare va reuşi vreodată să scape de ceea ce fuge? Sau a găsit în sfârşit un motiv să pună capăt acestei situaţii imposibile?

About the author

Jessica Cunsolo

17 books853 followers
Jessica Cunsolo’s young adult series, With Me, has amassed over 140 million reads on Wattpad since she posted her first story, She’s With Me, on the platform in 2015. It has won a Watty award, been published in multiple languages, and is in development for a feature film with Wattpad WEBTOON Studios. Jessica lives just outside of Toronto, where she enjoys the outdoors and transforming her real-life awkward situations into plotlines for her viral stories. You can find her on Instagram @jesscunsolo.

December 11, 2019
Terrific bully romance with a twist!



I love Bully romances because there is always so much going on in them. This is a classic example of that type of romance because it contains an alpha male character that is tall muscular and sexy but also broody and mean at times, that character is Aiden. Our hero in the standard bully romance is always surrounded by a small entourage of like minded individuals that take their cues from the Hero. We also have a heroine, Amelia that is constantly bullied, but is not afraid to stand up for herself.

Confident that my point was made and this jerk face was properly put in his place, I spin on my heel so my hair hits him on the shoulder and walk through the parting crowd, leaving him steaming.
“Oh my God, she so told you, Aiden! That was hilarious!” one of his gorgeous friends says through bursts of laughter.

The great thing about a lot of these books is that even though the Hero bullies the heroine, at some point they develop feelings for each other and he stops. Another thing I like is that there is usually another person willing and able to take up that bullying torch when our Hero puts it on the shelf. Whether that person is a former girlfriend of the Hero, the ex boyfriend of the heroine, some other character that was somehow rejected, or just someone with a grudge, the bullying often goes on.

I thought this book was a great example of the bully sub genre. I enjoyed it so much I couldn’t put it down and read it through in one sitting without breaks. There were some great secrets that both Aiden and Amelia are holding. And the reader finds them out gradually. Those secrets involve some sinister storylines which were really very good. I won’t spoil them but to say I liked how so much was going on and the storylines were well thought out and entertaining.

The characters were well developed and integrated nicely with the storylines. There were many different settings that were thoroughly described and it was a slow burn romance and very sweet. Though it is a young adult book where the majority of the characters are in high school, the book deals with some adult situations and may have some triggers for some people, such as fighting, violence against women, and abuse.

I voluntarily reviewed an advanced copy of this book. All thoughts and opinions are my own.

Sabía que podría gustarme, pero no tanto como lo ha hecho.
Es una historia que engancha desde el principio. Yo lo he escuchado, pero ahora mismo me voy a poner con el segundo que lo tengo en papel. Y es que en principio no me llamaba la atención, pero la editorial me mandó el segundo por sorpresa... nunca encontré el hueco para comprarme el primero, así que al verlo en Storytel me dije que esta era la mía y NI UN DÍA ME HA DURADO. No me podía despegar del teléfono jajaja
Creo que sin ninguna duda que en cuanto a audiolibros, es el que más me ha gustado de todos los que he escuchado, la narradora lo hace de 10 y me ha flipado. Ojalá estuviera también el segundo. Si tenéis la oportunidad, os recomiendo escuchar el audiolibro.
El caso, la historia nos habla sobre Amelia, una chica que llega nueva al instituto con un pasado oculto (que iremos descubriendo durante la novela) y ese primer día, se cruza con Aiden, el protagonista masculino de la novela, y tienen un encontronazo. Eso no quita que con el paso de los días, ambos se vayan conociendo mejor y se vayan haciendo amigos. Y Amelia no solo congenia con él, sino con su grupo de amigos, y la verdad es que la amistad es un punto muy importante en la historia. A partir de ahí veremos una tensión entre ellos, como van surgiendo los sentimientos, como se van descubriendo secretos de los personajes y también habrá mucho drama, como a mí me gusta.
La narración es muy sencilla, pero eso hace que la historia fluya muy bien.
La historia puede ser bastante cliché, pero como siempre digo, eso no tiene por qué ser malo. A mí me suelen gustar mucho este tipo de novelas del chico malo que no es tan malo y esconde un gran corazón y donde ambos personajes tienen un misterio detrás que te hace estar pegada a sus páginas (o en este caso, a mis cascos).
He cogido mucho cariño a todos los personajes. Creo que la amistad que se crea en esta novela es muy bonita y como todos lo dan todo por todos es maravilloso. Y me ha encantado ver, que aunque entre Amelia y Aiden hay tensión desde el principio, los sentimientos más grandes tardan en llegar.
Si os apetece leer una novela de instituto muy adictiva, con peligros y que os haga disfrutar, tenéis que darle una oportunidad.

First off, let's talk about how this novel is one HECK of a slow burn! I love slow burn romances and this story definitely was one. It was so slow that initially, I thought I was imagining a romance that wasn't even there.

This novel seemed to be different compared to a lot of other YA/NA novels that I read. I think it actually was the first novel that I've read that includes illegal racing and surprisingly enough, I loved that part of the story. It actually reminded me of "Fast and the Furious" (in the best way).

Along with the romance, this novel really excelled at showing a strong friend group. The loyalty between them all made the friendships that much more powerful and contributed to my overall enjoyment of the story. Hey, I'm a sucker for loyal and strong friendships.

This was such an easy novel to fly through and it left me wanting MORE! Seriously, talk about one heck of a painful ending. I cannot wait for the next novel in this series to be published!

3.5 Stars

Sometimes when the mood strikes, I go on Wattpad and read some YA stories. Anyone else who does this? 😂

Well, this particular story here is actually getting published in a few days and I got an ARC for the revised version, so a massive thanks to Smith Publicity Inc. and Netgalley for providing me with this copy!

Now how do I say this without sounding a bit "offensive"?
For a Wattpad story, this was actually pretty good!
It's definitely not for everyone though. This book is all about the "breathtaking" and "gorgeous" guy. Then, the overall voice of the book is a bit "juvenile", the heroine says things like "Of course I don't L word Aidan [...]" and the story has a lot of petty and cliché high school drama going on (= prank war with queen B) that went on too long imo, but you know what? Despite its issues, the story was quite addicting. It flowed very well and was easy to read.

I liked both MCs even though I had my doubts about Aidan because he didn't leave a very good first impression but I learned to love him. Then, Amelia was already interesting enough from the blurb alone (she's on the run and assumed a fake identity with the help of the FEDs), but the fact that she was fierce and a doer made me like her all the more. There's also the friendship in this book that has to be my favorite aspect of the story. Amelia found herself a tight-knit circle of friends (even though she wasn't supposed to) who were so much fun but were always there for her when it counted.

All in all, if you don't mind Wattpad (I'm saying/stressing this because I saw a lot of opposers on social media in the past) and are in the mood for some light reading, this could be it for you!

PS: Cliffhanger ending!


**ARC generously provided in exchange for an honest review. Thank you!

I received this book for free from in exchange for an honest review. This does not affect my opinion of the book or the content of my review.While scrolling through all the available ARCs on Netgalley, I came across this gem. I was hesitant at first as this is a debut novel and it is YA. The description really pulled me in, but there were a few more reasons why this captured my attention. This has been on Wattpad and manage to score over 100 million reads. It actually won a Watty award for Best Teen Fiction. Impressive, right? I thought so.

That description, though, was what captured my interest right off. It was giving me Penelope Douglas vibes - think Bully. It was also being compared, when I first picked it up, to the movie The Client. That was one of my favorite 90s movies, so I was intrigued to see what the correlation would be.

Amelia, the new girl in school, bumps into the school's bad boy, Aiden Parker. She becomes the talk of the school, something she is trying to avoid, when she puts him in his place for being a jerk. You see, Amelia has a past she's running from. Attention puts her at risk of being found. Getting mixed up with the notorious Aiden Parker isn't flying under the radar. But Aiden has demons of his own. Demons that set him apart from your average teenager. Are they the perfect match or the worst?

I'm going to toot my own horn and say that I was correct with all my assumptions. It did really give me Bully vibes as Aiden reminds me a lot of Jared. They also have similar hobbies. *hint-hint* Now that I've read it, why it was being compared to The Client. Although, I can also see why it isn't being marketed that way any longer because there is only ONE major plot point that relates to the movie. Nothing else. However, maybe they should have kept that comparison because it was one of my selling points.

A word of caution - this does end on a bit of a cliffhanger. If that bothers you, you may want to wait until the next installment is available before diving in. And, trust me, you'll want to dive in.

My final thoughts? It is a really enjoyable read. I highly recommend it to those who love a over-the-top high school romance with a dash of suspense and very low steam.

A special thanks to Netgalley and Wattpad Books for providing me with an advanced readers copy for review! xxThis review was originally posted on Sincerely, Whitney

ATTN: I’d also like to mention again that I rate books based on their genre, so this rating is compared to other books IN THE SAME GENRE!! (So in this case vs other YA romances)

Like 2.6, but I can’t give it a 3.

There was too much going on, but also it was a little too slow all at the same time?? There was so much stuffed in the final 30 pages, so many open storylines and unanswered questions. I understand that this is part of a trilogy, but a few loose ends could have been tied up.

There is plenty of the “forced proximity” trope in this one. So if that’s your jam, something to keep in mind. Instead of just the brooding bad boy, there was a mild bully romance trope in this one and that’s just not my personal favourite.

The amount of characters made it difficult to develop any of their storylines. I wanted to learn more about them, but there wasn’t enough time to get to genuinely learn about them.

It was still a quick read and it had a few interesting storylines to peak my interest, but I don’t feel like it measures up to the Sarah Dessen or the Katie Cotugno or the Jenny Han books, which are within the same genre!

Sadly, I don’t think I will be continuing this series.

A new town, a new love, another chance to stay alive. Arriving in another new town, Amelia Collins vows to fit in and finish her senior year drama free. There can’t be any mistakes. But when she’s befriended by a group of students who make her feel safe and loved, Amelia struggles to maintain her distance, especially when faced with her feelings for Aiden Parker, who weaken her resolve. I was given a free copy of this book by the author. This in no way affects my opinion. I try to express only my most honest opinion in a spoiler-free way. If you feel anything in my review is a spoiler and is not already hidden in spoiler brackets please let me know. Thank you.

I'm giving this book a 4 star because I really enjoyed the story, but I didn't feel the drive to read it as much as I would have expected. And what's with the cover? I don't know about anyone else, but it looks like two girls on the cover, and this is not an LGBT romance. I wouldn't care either way as I love all forms of romance books, but still, it's confusing.

I love the close connection that all the friends in this book have. I love the characters and how they all have such different personalities. Even the 'mean girl' in the story is unique in the fact that she is completely crazy lol. I love the romance in the story of course, but I also like that there was a hint of a love triangle without it going full-on angsty. I'm all for a good love triangle, but it has to be done right.

Few things I didn't like. There where some parts that made me roll my eyes. Some of the dialogue was not really believable to me, and although I'm all for having a fighting spirit. She was big on antagonizing others until she finally wised up about that. And the whole reason that she was in witness protection feels wrong. I know its possible as people do awful things for no reason. But the fact that this Tony would blame her doesn't make any sense at all.

The book ended on a HUGE cliffhanger and left so many things unresolved. I have to have more and plan to continue the series cause I have to know what happens next.

How I choose my rating:
1* Hated it. I had to force myself to finish it.
2** Didn't like it. I didn't hate it but not sure why I finished it other than for some closure.
